While running a custom process that performs many Fedora reads (including retrieval of RDF in XML format), I encountered an intermittent problem with a java.lang.IllegalStateException being thrown. This occurred 32 times over the course of 3 days, at a time when at least 600,000 requests were made. Retrying always succeeded, so the problem was intermittent – presumably related to system resources rather than specific data.
See an example backtrace in the attached trace.txt for more details.

comments.body: Looks a little like https://bugs.java.com/bugdatabase/view_bug.do?bug_id=6712096 which suggests that the issue could be correlated with a lack of available disk space.

Danny Bernstein, while I did encounter some disk space problems during my test, I continued to see these errors after all of them were resolved. I can’t completely rule out the possibility of lack of disk space, but it doesn’t seem likely to account for all 32 instances that I encountered (unless Fedora is using the system tmp directory, and these instances happened to correlate with multiple processes simultaneously dropping huge temporary files there, which I guess is conceivable, but doesn’t feel likely).

From Peter Winckles in Slack

The issue here is that there's an encoder being used as a singleton, but it's actually not thread-safe. Per the javadoc in CharsetEncoder:

Instances of this class are not safe for use by multiple concurrent threads.
Here's a built version for you so to don't have to build yourself (see attached war and jetty console jar)

Thanks, Danny Bernstein! I’ve just queued up an index job of 100,000 PIDs. Based on past performance, that should trigger at least 5 errors if the bug still exists. I’ll let you know tomorrow how it turns out.

Danny Bernstein , I’m prepared to declare victory here. I ran your updated Fedora .jar and bombarded it for 24 hours with 100,000 reindexing requests (each of which triggers many Fedora calls). Not a single failure, whereas previously this would definitely have encountered the 500 error described by this ticket.

Hooray! Thank you for verifying it Demian Katz.

Resolved by https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/commit/1f23159329183fd0ade217956e0a4482be515497
